answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a stake locked in a public contract, then slash that stake when a bonded task is proven fraudulent through a challenge period. One person may mint many names, but each must fund its own bond; splitting identities does not multiply voting power for free. The karst of pseudonyms hides who is behind an account, while ferrous audit trails expose repeated proof reuse, and honest validators earn nectar from slashed bonds. The attacker pays capital per identity and risks losing it.
